issues.legal_issue: Whether the claimant established title to the disputed property on the basis of revenue entries and the other evidence relied upon.
material_facts: The claimant relied on three revenue entries from one year that recorded it as the cultivator of the land.
Revenue records spanning many years, including settlement and patta records, consistently recorded the temple’s archakas as pattadars or grantees of the land.
A village petition seeking recognition of the deity’s claim had been rejected by the revenue authority.

An earlier judgment had found the land belonged to the temple, but that finding was not challenged in the appeal from that judgment; the suit was dismissed because the plaintiff lacked standing to seek possession.
The oral evidence was uncertain and inadequate to displace the effect of the long course of revenue entries.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not establish title to the disputed property. The appeal was dismissed and the High Court’s judgment was confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Revenue entries may be considered as evidence of title and possession, but isolated entries do not outweigh a consistent course of entries over many years. An earlier judgment’s finding on ownership cannot support the claim where that finding was not contested in the appeal from that judgment. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: title_or_possession_appeal and long_consistent_records_favor_occupants and isolated_record_favors_claimant and oral_evidence_inconclusive

predicates.title_or_possession_appeal: A party appeals in a dispute seeking recognition of title to, or possession of, property.
predicates.long_consistent_records_favor_occupants: Records maintained over many years consistently identify the persons in possession as owners, pattadars, or grantees of the property.
predicates.isolated_record_favors_claimant: One or a few records from a limited period identify the claimant as owner or cultivator of the property.
predicates.oral_evidence_inconclusive: The oral evidence is uncertain and does not adequately counter the documentary record.
predicates.claimant_title_not_established: The claimant has not proved title to the property.

issues.definition: When a party appeals in a property title or possession dispute, long-standing records favoring the occupants outweigh isolated records favoring the claimant if the oral evidence is inconclusive, and the claimant's title is not established.
